720	Once I gave a talk in the United States, and there was an American there
721	who really loved the talk, so he said
722	to me, "Rabbi, what a beautiful talk, ashrecha!" Then another American came up next to him and said
723	to him, "Ashrecha!"
724	Then they asked me how you say "ashrecha"
725	in English. Now how would I know how to say
726	"ashrecha" in English? I said to him,
727	"Ashrecha." How do you say "ashrecha" in English? "Ashrecha" is
728	all there is. There was once someone who became fully
729	a baal teshuvah. You know, baalei teshuvah, everything
730	is "ashrecha, ashrecha, ashreichem." You don't
731	know what you want from him. "Ashrecha, ashrecha,
732	ashreichem." So he went into a gas station to fill up,
733	and as soon as he went in to fill up, there was an Arab
734	who told him, "Open the window." So he opened the
735	window, and he says to him, "Cash?"
736	He says to him, the Arab asks him, "Credit?" So he
737	says to him, "Ashrecha, ashrecha, everything is ashrecha." Fine, in any
738	case, the whole idea here is that in the end, He tells him:
739	"And I brought you, I brought you to the Land of Israel, a land which
740	HaShem your Elokim looks after, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year." What
741	is "from the beginning of the year to the end of the year"? That every moment there is
742	individual Divine providence over a person in the Land of Israel. All
743	the land flowing with milk and honey. The whole idea is that in the Land of
744	Israel there are seven species: olive oil and date honey, wheat, barley,
745	pomegranate. It all hints at sefirot that exist in the Land of Israel,
746	where one can rise higher. How important it is to be in the Land of
747	Israel, because a person who truly learns Torah rises
748	here much more than he rises outside the Land.
749	I received many levels of holiness outside the Land, and there were
750	many times outside the Land when I worked very hard on
751	Torah, no less than I worked in the Land of Israel. There was
752	one year in the United States, even before I was a rabbi,
753	when they offered me a lot of money to spend two days at a
754	community in Miami: 3,000 dollars. They told me, "Come
755	with us, just for Rosh HaShanah."
756	Now, 3,000 dollars, I had no money and I really
757	needed it. But then, how am I
758	going to pray with people like that, who talk, who don't
759	talk during the prayer, who make trouble and so on? So what
760	did I do? I told them, "I don't agree. I want
761	to go pray in a yeshivah." And I gave up on the money,
762	and I went and prayed in the yeshivah on 41st Street, in the yeshivah
763	of Rabbi Zweig in Miami Beach, a yeshivah of Torah students,
764	black-hat types, serious about prayer. But
765	I asked them to give me a bed to sleep in, and they didn't
766	give me even a bed. There was no bed. I told
767	them, "I'm willing to pay, give me a bed." Not even a bed.
768	And I didn't know people, and back then I wasn't
769	Rabbi Meir Eliyahu. Today people know me
770	there in the street, but back then I was just Meir, I was not
771	anybody, and I had nowhere to sleep. And what was it?
772	I wanted to pray in this yeshivah on Rosh HaShanah. I said,
773	"I gave up 3,000 dollars, I want to pray
774	in this yeshivah." And there was nowhere to sleep, and they also didn't
775	want to leave the beit midrash open all night. They
776	lock the beit midrash. So what did I do in order
777	to pray in the yeshivah? After it ended, before it ended,
778	before Aleinu LeShabe'ach, I went into the restroom and locked
779	the restroom, and they closed up the yeshivah, and I didn't want
780	them to look for me, in case they looked for me. So what I did was
781	lock the restroom, and I slept in the restroom on
782	the floor. And that's how I spent that Rosh HaShanah. I
783	spent it in the restroom on the floor. I took the trash can,
784	turned it over, and that was my pillow. HaShem knows
785	that I'm telling this only so that you can see mesirut
786	nefesh. And I closed, I closed the door,
787	I locked it. It was a single restroom, like a, Heaven forbid,
788	a single restroom. I closed the door and put myself there all
789	night.
790	It was cold and my back broke, and I got up with back pain,
791	and my whole body was broken, and I couldn't concentrate
792	very much in the prayers because of all the back pain I had
793	all of Rosh HaShanah. And that very year I merited levels
794	of holiness that I had not merited in all the years since I became
795	a baal teshuvah. And what levels
796	I received that year, levels of holiness, something that couldn't
797	be missed. And also for giving up that money,
798	HaShem granted me that year to find work,
799	and I was the rabbi of a community, and everything fell into place, and I rose,
800	and I wrote most of the book Merkavot Argaman on the Torah
801	that year, and I also wrote part one of Sasson
802	that year, and everything fell into place, and that same year I also merited, at the end,
803	to make aliyah to the Land of Israel. So, so, so the mesirut nefesh
804	that a person gives for the mitzvot of the Holy One, blessed be He,
805	He does not forget it. I'm not saying this so
806	that you'll owe me thanks for sleeping on a restroom floor,
807	but only to say that if you want something, you
808	have to give of yourself. There's no such thing as getting it free. If
809	you want something, the Holy One, blessed be He, will give you, but
810	you have to give back. You only ask: give me, give me, bring
811	me, take for me, do for me. And what do you give in return?
812	After all, that's how it is in this country: one hand washes the other. You
813	help me with National Insurance, I'll help you with the
814	property tax. You help me with the mortgage, I'll help
815	you with your mother-in-law. I know what, each one
816	helps with what he needs to. That's not how it works. If you
817	give, HaShem gives. Don't expect that the Holy One, blessed be
818	He, will give you for free. People think that the Holy One,
819	blessed be He, works for them: give me, take for me, do
820	for me, bring me. What works for you? You love what's his,
821	not love what's yours, to compare, Heaven forbid. So if you
822	want the Holy One, blessed be He, to truly look at you
823	and give to you, you must give back. When was the last time
824	you gave tzedakah that hurt your pocket? When was the last time
825	you fasted and it hurt your body? When was the last time
826	you sat and shut off your phone, and it hurt you to shut
827	off your phone, you stayed silent and it hurt you to stay silent? People
828	simply don't know what a reality of sacrifice is.
829	Avraham Avinu slaughtered his son. Why did he slaughter
830	his son? Why do we read about it every day?
831	Mesirut nefesh. And so too Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who was
832	in the cave all those years, 13 years. Why to this day
833	do we remember Rashbi more than all the Tannaim? Mesirut
834	nefesh. He slept on the floor 13 years, not one night,
835	13 years he was on the floor, 13 years he ate
836	carobs that ruin the stomach, they are like swords
837	to the stomach, he and Rabbi Elazar his son. And therefore both are buried
838	inside the cave. The cave did not accept anyone after
839	the two of them. Later they commanded to bury the grandson of Rashbi
